newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson seen raising Great Western bid.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson seen raising Great Western bid.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co is likely to raise its bid for Great Western Financial Corp following a rival offer by Washington Mutual Savings Bank, analysts and arbitrageurs said Thursday.
"It's unlikely that their first bid would be their last bid," said Steven Cohen, research director at Kellner, DiLeo and Co, a money management firm.

Ahmanson said today it was still committed to its merger proposal and believed there would be a negative reaction in the stock market to the merger pact announced this morning by Great Western and Washington Mutual.
But Washington Mutual shares were up 2-3/8 to 55-1/2, and Great Western was up 2-7/8 to 47-7/8.
The Washington Mutual-Great Western pact calls for the tax-free exchange of 0.9 share of Washington Mutual for each share of Great Western.
Based on Thursday stock market prices, the ratio represents an offer of $50.06 a share for Great Western.
Ahmanson is proposing to exchange 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share, placing a value of $43.32 per share on Great Western.
Ahmanson was down 7/8 to 41-1/8 this morning.
"The leg-up in a situation like this is normally with the friendly bidder," said Cohen. "They've bid higher and have the blessing of the (Great Western) board."
Another takeover specialist said Ahmanson can wait several weeks before making its next move.
"They may eventually raise the bid, but it depends on what happens with Washington Mutual's stock. This deal is not closing right away," said the specialist.
Arbitrageurs said Ahmanson could easily afford to raise its bid for Great Western, given the cost savings it could wring from a merger.

"Washington Mutual told everyone they were interested in California, so this (merger oact with Great Western) is no surprise," said an arbitrageur who declined to be named. "It is a pretty full bid and stretches Washington a bit."
He added, "But I believe Ahmanson can pay more, eventually squeezing out a few more million for the deal."
